blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Possible retained: DOC is a permissionless rBTC CDP with no holder-balance freeze or blacklist on the token, but the Money On Chain contract suite is DAO-governed and proxy-upgradeable, leaving an indirect intervention surface.

oracleRisk.summary: Money On Chain uses a decentralized oracle/medianizer process for BTC/USD reference pricing, but reviewed sources do not show a stronger failover tier.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: DOC is natively a Rootstock rBTC-collateralized CDP stablecoin; its Arbitrum deployment (0x2ad62eb9...) is a self-deployed LayerZero V2 OFT representation (contract name "MyOFT", canonical LZ endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c, ~37K DOC max supply). Money On Chain's own announcement (moneyonchain.com/doc-arbitrum) states DOC moves between Rootstock and Arbitrum via Stargate/LayerZero — a generic-OFT lock/mint route with a third-party (LayerZero) control surface, not the Arbitrum canonical bridge and not a Stargate canonical Hydra pool asset. This refutes the L2BEAT "Arbitrum Canonical" seed.

protocols.name: Money On Chain — DOC on Arbitrum announcement (Stargate route)
protocols.note: Issuer states DOC moves Rootstock<>Arbitrum via Stargate (LayerZero), not a proprietary or canonical bridge.

protocols.name: Arbiscan — DOC Arbitrum token contract (LayerZero V2 OFT)
protocols.note: Verified contract 'MyOFT' on LZ endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c; owner-controlled peers/delegates, cross-chain mint/burn. Arbitrum supply is a minted OFT representation.

protocols.name: Stargate Hydra docs (Pool-to-OFT lock/mint)
protocols.note: Hydra locks native asset on source chain (Protocol Locked Liquidity) and mints an OFT representation on the destination — an OFT-adapter lock/mint pattern.
